symptoms.title: Yellowing from older leaves
symptoms.description: Yellowing usually starts along the margins of older lower leaves, then progresses toward the midrib and younger leaves.

symptoms.title: Wilting and leaf collapse
symptoms.description: Leaf stalks may buckle, and collapsed older leaves can form a skirt around the pseudostem while a few young leaves remain upright.

symptoms.title: Internal vascular discoloration
symptoms.description: A cut pseudostem or corm may show yellow, reddish-brown, or dark-brown discoloration in the water-conducting tissue.

symptoms.title: Splitting and plant decline
symptoms.description: Some plants develop lengthwise splitting near the pseudostem base, followed by progressive wilt, decline, and death.

treatment.title: Do not disturb the suspected plant
treatment.description: Do not uproot, cut, or move the plant, suckers, or surrounding soil. Stop people, tools, footwear, water, and vehicles from carrying soil to another part of the farm.

treatment.title: Isolate the area
treatment.description: Mark the location, restrict entry, and prevent rainwater or irrigation runoff from leaving the suspected area. Clean visible soil from footwear and equipment without spreading it.

treatment.title: Contact the Sto. Tomas City Agriculture Office
treatment.description: Request confirmation and containment instructions at (043) 784-8022 local 307 or agri@cityofstotomas.gov.ph. The office is at the Basement Floor, City Hall Main Building, Gov. Malvar Street, Poblacion I.

treatment.title: There is no curative fungicide
treatment.description: Fungicides do not cure Panama Disease. Do not destroy or chemically treat a suspected plant until the agriculture or plant-health authority provides instructions.

prevention.title: Use certified clean plants
prevention.description: Plant disease-free tissue-culture plants or other material from a trusted, traceable source. Never obtain suckers from a field with unexplained wilting.

prevention.title: Keep soil from moving
prevention.description: Limit farm entry and remove soil from boots, tools, tires, and equipment before moving between plots. Keep dedicated tools for suspect areas.

prevention.title: Control water movement
prevention.description: Maintain drainage and prevent runoff or floodwater from carrying soil from a suspect area into clean plantings, especially during heavy Batangas rains.

prevention.title: Plan with the City Agriculture Office
prevention.description: Ask the Sto. Tomas City Agriculture Office which resistant or tolerant cultivars and containment practices are appropriate before replanting.
